solves.reasoning: (A) competing ideas in a marketplace of ideas, (B) statements to justify those beliefs, (C) treating language with greater respect
(A) evaluate them for best fit to reality, (B) But in practice contrasts 'in theory', (C) we can achieve more than simple self-defense
(A) facts form the basis of our beliefs, (B) we are not seeking statements as facts, (C) Language might be good for this function
③ abandon(버리다) contradicts context: we seek statements to justify (not abandon) beliefs. Other markers encounter/beliefs/achieve match original.
② worst contradicts: evaluate for their best (not worst) fit to reality. knowledge/shop/treating all match original.
④ lesser contradicts: By treating language with greater (not lesser) respect, we can achieve more. classical/stories/figure out all match original text.
form the basis of our ___ → beliefs; the best facts form the foundation of what we believe
their best fit to ___ → reality; evaluating ideas against reality is the scientist's way
a market for ___ → justifications; contrasts earlier 'market for ideas', we seek justifications not ideas
encounter = come across (마주치다). avoid is antonym, create/reject are unrelated.
evaluate = assess (평가하다). ignore is antonym, collect/distribute are unrelated actions.
achieve = accomplish (달성하다/성취하다). prevent is antonym, attempt/desire are different meanings.
competing (경쟁하는) ↔ cooperating (협력하는). rivaling/contending/clashing are all synonyms of competing.
brightest (가장 뛰어난/밝은) ↔ dullest (가장 둔한). smartest/sharpest are synonyms. boldest is different semantic axis (courage).
(A) figure out = 알아내다 (phrasal verb in context 'help us figure out what'), (B) drew every figure = 형상/인물 (noun, physical form in painting)
'explanation or reason given to show that an action or belief is right or reasonable' = justification. criticism=비판, statement=진술(too broad), accusation=비난
as ___ (think) individuals → adjective/participle needed before noun → thinking (현재분사/형용사)
seeking ___ (state) as facts → plural noun needed as direct object → statements (진술들)
facts form ___ our beliefs → the basis of; collocation 'form the basis of' = 토대를 형성하다
they contain ___ → stories about ideas; passage explicitly contrasts 'contain ideas' vs 'contain stories about ideas'
